question: Which of the following best describes a 'business model'?
before: A business model encompasses the entire value creation and capture mechanism — value proposition, revenue model, cost structure, and competitive moat. Option A is only the product. C is only go-to-market. D is internal structure.
after:
Concept: A business model is the integrated framework that describes how a company identifies customer needs, designs and delivers solutions, and establishes revenue streams to achieve profitability and growth. It connects product, delivery, pricing, and cost management into a coherent system.

Why this is correct: Option B captures the full scope—it is not just what a company makes or how it organises itself, but the entire mechanism of value creation (identifying and solving customer problems), value delivery (channels and customer experience), and value capture (revenue and profit realisation). This is the definition used in equity research when analysts assess company viability and competitive positioning.

Why the others are wrong: Option A (product) identifies only what is sold, not how it generates profit or reaches customers—a product alone is not a business model. Option C (marketing strategy) is a tactical execution component within a business model, not the business model itself. Option D (organisational structure) describes internal hierarchy and reporting lines, which are separate from the mechanism of creating and capturing value.

Intuition: In equity research, understanding a company's business model is foundational—it reveals *how* the company makes money and *why* it can sustain competitive advantage. A stock analyst must assess whether the model is defensible and scalable before valuing the business; two companies selling identical products can have vastly different business models and investment merit.
